topic: Flow Shock and Comet intensity ribbon variants
objective: Render Flow Shock and Comet Speed Density as compact historical ribbons with dark-chart directional palettes and causal percentile-driven intensity grading without changing their research-state rules.
unresolved_questions: Do MMT historical trade replay and live updates produce the same ribbon path for both variants?
Does the two-line Flow Shock view reveal useful opposing-side structure without obscuring the original dominant-side score?
Are the Comet drive and density traces visually separable across quiet and liquidation-heavy sessions?
Do the default opacity curve and palette preserve weak-state visibility without making ordinary observations look exceptional?
Do any descriptive states predict executable outcomes after matched controls and costs?

debate.thesis: Causal percentile values can support a compact graded ribbon that improves historical state comparison without changing the underlying detector or implying new predictive information.
debate.strongest_support: Both indicators already maintain prior-only rolling baselines, so ribbon height and intensity can be driven by existing normalized measurements rather than hindsight scaling.
debate.strongest_objection: A polished, bright ribbon can create false salience, and trade-only active-second history may not reconstruct continuously or identically in MMT replay.
debate.belief_update: Two visual-only variants now use wide glow plus crisp core lines and Ice & Ember magnitude grading. Flow Shock exposes buy and sell scores while preserving the dominant-side score; Comet keeps drive and density separate. No signal rule, evidence grade, or strategy claim was promoted, and platform compile plus replay remain required.

last_query: Turn Flow Shock and Comet Density into reference-like ribbons with an intensity-graded color palette.
